scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

F-01.statement: Manual-read route completion was 0.88 (target 0.95) for 9200 manual-read accounts over the 2026-08..09 period.

F-02.statement: The tariff_change_log in billing-db has 0 records, ruling out tariff rate changes as a cause of the billing errors.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025).

F-04.statement: CRM dispute response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 authorizes the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 records with per-route completion values; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts were billed on an ESTIMATED read last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (E-10).

F-09.statement: mdms-export AMI read-event data for the 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts: 1184 had a before-cutoff read exported to billing but rejected import status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 had no AMI read received (NO_READ_RECEIVED).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume is driven mainly by slow/inadequate ticket handling, so an AI agent that auto-answers disputes and auto-corrects bills will bring volume back to baseline.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused systematic bill errors (e.g., altered estimate-substitution thresholds), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI) degraded since August, increasing estimate substitution and causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter-read completion dropped since August (e.g., due to staffing), increasing estimated bills and disputes.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-DEFECT.statement: The 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself produces systematically wrong bills regardless of upstream read-delivery quality.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-DEFECT.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) involve ACTUAL, non-estimated reads, suggesting a billing-side defect (e.g., import, calculation, or validation issue) independent of read-collection failures is driving most disputes.

H-IMPORT-REJECTS-HIGH-CONSUMPT.statement: Billing import rejects valid, before-cutoff AMI reads flagged HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1184 of 1240 AMI-channel ESTIMATED-dispute accounts, E-12), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills, independent of true AMI read-collection failure (only 56 cases).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field route-completion log shows manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, during the Aug–Sep 2026 period in which dispute tickets doubled — indicating a field read-collection shortfall coinciding with the dispute surge.

Observation still shows manual-read route completion at 88% (target 95%) across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (unchanged), but it no longer means a field read-collection shortfall drives the dominant dispute mechanism: E-12 shows 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED disputes arise from billing-import rejecting valid, before-cutoff AMI reads, not from missed field/AMI collection, so the timing coincidence does not establish field staffing as a cause of the dominant surge mechanism.
billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes were logged that could independently explain the wrong bills behind the dispute surge.

The billing-db breakdown shows 1785 disputed bills had ACTUAL reads versus 1240 with ESTIMATED reads, so disputed bills are majority ACTUAL-read, not ESTIMATED-read. This means estimate substitution (from failed AMI or field reads) cannot be the dominant driver of the dispute surge, since most disputed bills were not estimates at all.

re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (39% of all disputes) are also caused by a billing import/validation defect (HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection), not by field/AMI collection failure as implied; the root premise's narrow framing of the defect as 'turning accepted actual reads into wrong bills' undercounts the mechanism's true reach into the ESTIMATED-dispute bucket.; PR-CHAIN-2: The premise dismisses 'estimate substitution' as not dominant, but E-12 shows estimate substitution (triggered by import rejection, not missed reads) is in fact the dominant outcome for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-dispute accounts, a large share of total disputes.

CRM dispute response times (2440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, meaning ticket handling speed is currently within target despite the ticket-volume surge, not lagging.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is an unverified stakeholder statement that happens to agree with the existing authoritative tariff_change_log result (E-02, value false), but adds no new decision-relevant information beyond that already-ruled-out explanation.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (an interested party seeking headcount increase) claims a shortfall of three readers since July has caused routes to run late, producing estimated bills for the affected customers; this is an unverified, non-authoritative stakeholder statement offering a causal mechanism, not new measured evidence, and it does not address why most disputed bills are ACTUAL-read (E-03) rather than estimated.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) tickets: volume roughly doubled from July to August and continued rising into September rather than reverting. This confirms the magnitude of the surge cited in the initial request but is a volume-trend record only — it does not identify which causal mechanism (read type, staffing, rules, tariff) drives the surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) states the utility may request field route priority changes but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation. This corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update; it has no bearing on the billing-side defect causing the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes provides a per-route breakdown underlying the aggregate 88% completion figure (E-01): 14 distinct routes are lagging, with the sampled route R-00 at 0.70 completion. This adds granularity to the known field route-completion shortfall but, standing alone, does not link lagging routes to specific disputed accounts or to the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-03), so it does not by itself establish the field-completion-to-dispute correlation that U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB asks about.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) is a raw list of 320 accounts that received an ESTIMATED read last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes. It is a precursor dataset for the pending correlate_estimated_disputes_with_route_completion work item but by itself does not compute any overlap with the 14 lagging routes (E-09) or the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-03), so it does not yet establish or refute the field-completion-to-dispute link.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side stakeholder) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would lift the ACCESS_PENDING hold that previously blocked mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated and the request_vendor_ami_read_access:DA-MDMS scope item. This is an unverified vendor stakeholder statement, not a tool-confirmed state change, and mdms-export tool_health is still recorded as DEGRADED independent of this access claim.

AMI read-event data for the 1240 AMI-channel disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts shows 1184 had a valid read received before the billing cutoff and exported to billing, yet were rejected by billing import under a HIGH_CONSUMPTION status; only 56 truly had no AMI read received. This points to a billing import validation rule rejecting legitimate high-consumption AMI reads — not AMI/field read-collection failure — as the dominant cause of the ESTIMATED-read disputes.

U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: Which specific billing-side defect (import validation rule change, estimate-substitution logic fault, or other calculation error) is producing wrong bills for ACTUAL-read accounts?
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines which system/config component must be corrected and whether any bill-correction write-back is needed, shaping the eventual fix design.
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule_change_log and billing-db import/calculation records for changes coinciding with the August onset.
U-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Continue root-cause analysis via read-only billing-config and billing-db queries; do not design or deploy any automated bill-correction fix until the defect locus is confirmed.

U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB.question: Does the field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-01) explain the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-03) as a secondary contributing factor?
U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB.decision_impact: If confirmed, field staffing/route completion is a secondary fix track separate from the dominant billing-side defect; if not, the staffing claim (E-06) may be unrelated to disputes.
U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion records for the 9200 manual-read accounts against the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed-bill accounts.
U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB.safe_placeholder: Treat field staffing as a secondary, unconfirmed contributor; do not base headcount or dispatch decisions on it yet.
U-ESTIMATED-MINOR-CONTRIB.resolution: E-12's 1184+56=1240 count exactly matches E-03's ESTIMATED-dispute total and all are AMI-channel, so the manual-read field route-completion shortfall (E-01) does not explain the ESTIMATED-read disputes; the cause is billing import rejection of valid AMI reads, not field read failure.

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.question: What does AMI read event data (DA-MDMS) show about read quality/delivery for disputed accounts, given vendor mdms-export access is currently pending (ACCESS_PENDING hold)?
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Without this data, AMI-side read-value corruption (distinct from missing-read estimate substitution) cannot be fully ruled out as a contributing factor.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Escalate to ORG-AMI vendor to provision mdms-export access; retry the read_events_for_disputed_estimated query once granted.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-side defect analysis using available billing-db/billing-config/route-log data; defer any AMI-read-quality conclusion until export access is restored.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: mdms-export returned complete, authoritative AMI read-event data for disputed ESTIMATED accounts (E-12): access is now functioning, and AMI read quality itself is largely intact (1184/1240 reads received before cutoff), with rejection happening downstream in billing import, not in AMI delivery.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.question: Is monthly dispute ticket volume (E-07) a valid sole proxy for 'bills are correct' (G-1), or could it include disputes unrelated to the actual-read billing defect?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether success should be measured by ticket-volume reduction alone or jointly with a direct billing-accuracy metric.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Once the defect is identified, track both dispute volume and a direct error-rate metric (e.g., ACTUAL-read dispute share) to confirm volume reduction coincides with the fix.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-PROXY-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report dispute-volume trend and ACTUAL-read dispute share as paired success indicators rather than relying on volume alone.

A-SINGLE-DEFECT-LOCUS.statement: The billing-side defect causing wrong bills for ACTUAL-read accounts is concentrated in one step (import/calculation/validation) rather than several independent faults.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MINOR.statement: The field route-completion shortfall (E-01) and the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-03) are a secondary, non-dominant contributor to the surge rather than a coinciding root cause.

A-VOLUME-REFLECTS-ERRORS.statement: Rising dispute ticket volume (E-07) tracks growth in actual billing errors rather than an independent rise in contact propensity, since response handling stays within SLA (E-04).

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

K-BILLWRITE.description: Writes to customer bills (re-bill, credit) require Billing Operations authority; no automated bill writes.

SC-NO-UNAUTHORIZED-WRITES.validation_method: Enforce K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH protected-action gating on write_bill_adjustment and push_route_update before any such action executes.

SC-VOLUME-BASELINE.validation_method: Monitor crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly for at least two consecutive months after the fix.
